thread:
mia: hi all, first day q  redis in docker-compose doesn't accept connections from the app service. compose has redis:6379 mapped, but the app gets ConnectionRefused.

mia: logs from redis: ```redis_1  | 1:C 23 Mar 2026 10:12:34.123 # Warning: no config file specified, using the default config.
redis_1  | 1:M 23 Mar 2026 10:12:34.124 * Running mode=standalone, port=6379.
redis_1  | 1:M 23 Mar 2026 10:12:34.125 # Server initialized
```

sam: welcome @mia! a few things to check: is your app using hostnames or localhost? In compose the service should use the service name (redis) as host. Also check network_mode or extra_hosts.

sam: paste your compose snippet?

mia: snippet: ```yaml
services:
  app:
    build: .
    depends_on: [redis]
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
  redis:
    image: redis:7
```

sam: aha  that's the issue. REDIS_URL should point to redis://redis:6379 not localhost, because localhost inside the app container is the container itself. Change env to redis://redis:6379 and it should connect.

mia: changed env and now connection works, thanks! also fyi i hit volume permission error when mounting ./redis-data on mac: ```redis_1  | Can't save RDB: Permission denied```

infra-bot: note: on macOS Docker Desktop, bind-mounted dirs can have permission quirks. options: use a named volume, or ensure the host dir is accessible to Docker (Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources > File Sharing).

sam: good call. if you need to inspect redis dump files on host, run redis as a sidecar that writes to a named volume and use a temporary container to copy files out.

mia: thanks everyone  all set. devex: could you add a one-liner to the new-hire checklist about using service hostnames?

devex: on it, adding a note and example compose envs. welcome again! :tada:
